evidence: src/domain/Order.ts: advanceTo calls nextFulfilmentState(...) and cancel calls isCancellable(...) from OrderState.ts; the transition rules are not copied into Order.
src/domain/OrderState.ts: FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE and CANCELLABLE_STATES are the only definitions of the order lifecycle.
src/domain/Quantity.ts: Quantity.of enforces the positive-integer rule; OrderLine and Product take Quantity rather than raw numbers.
src/domain/Product.ts: canReserve/available is the single stock-availability rule, and assertReserved is the single rule for releasing or dispatching reserved units.

src/domain/StockReservationService.ts: reserve() checks every line up front using product.canReserve and product.available, then applies through product.reserve/release/dispatch and saves via ProductRepository. Products are never changed directly.
src/domain/errors.ts: every domain error extends DomainError and is used consistently across Order, Product, Quantity and StockReservationService.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
src/domain is one cohesive order-fulfilment and stock domain. It holds the aggregates (Order, Product), value objects (Quantity, OrderLine, OrderState), repository ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository), one domain service (StockReservationService) and a shared error hierarchy (errors.ts). Each invariant has a single home:
- Order state transitions live in OrderState.ts (FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE, CANCELLABLE_STATES), and Order.ts only calls nextFulfilmentState and isCancellable.
- The rule that a quantity must be a positive integer lives in Quantity.of.
- The stock-availability rule lives in Product.canReserve and Product.available.
- The rule that you can only release or dispatch units that are reserved lives in Product.assertReserved.
StockReservationService.reserve checks availability for every line before changing anything, so it is all-or-nothing. It calls product.canReserve and reads product.available rather than re-deriving onHand - reserved, so it uses the Product abstraction instead of bypassing it. The only repetition is that it builds the same InsufficientStockError that Product.reserve throws, which is minor. Product.create's check that stock on hand is a non-negative integer is a different invariant from Quantity's positive-integer rule, because zero stock is allowed, so it is not a duplicate. Quantity.add uses the private constructor directly, but adding two positive integers always gives a positive integer, so no invariant is skipped. One thing outside the rubric: the service's doc comment says every movement validates all lines first, but release and dispatch only validate each line inside Product as they go, so they can apply part of a batch before failing. That is a correctness gap, not a cohesion or duplication problem.
